A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Causal-Adapter work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or reformatted in v4.

before.justification: V1 reports original quantitative and qualitative counterfactual-generation results on Pendulum, CelebA, and ADNI, together with motivational experiments and ablations.

after.justification: V4 retains original empirical results and adds CelebA-HQ experiments, SD3 evaluations, compositional interventions, and causal-structure learning results.

M1.justification: The original SCM, frozen SD1.5 adapter, PAI, and CTC remain. Appendix E.4 adds an SD3 adaptation using three text-embedding streams, flow-matching loss, and inversion-free FlowEdit inference. Appendix G adds an optional learnable adjacency matrix with an acyclicity penalty. These extend the actual training and inference procedures.

E1.justification: V4 adds CelebA-HQ with glasses, smiling, and mouth-opening interventions, additional conditioning attributes, and progressively combined interventions. It also evaluates causal-graph recovery on the three retained datasets. This expands both attribute coverage and task requirements beyond v1's counterfactual-generation evaluations.

E2.justification: The original benchmark comparator sets remain. V4 adds evaluated comparisons with VCI and DiffCounter on CelebA-HQ, alongside HVAE (Tables 4 and 14), and with SDCD, NOTEARS, and DAGMA for graph recovery (Figure 34). Several were only cited, or absent, in v1.

E3.justification: V4 introduces CelebA-HQ splits and training settings, including four additional conditioning attributes, plus SD3 evaluation. It adds reversal L1 and intervention-to-original LPIPS measurements, distinct from existing null-intervention reconstruction metrics. Graph discovery adds a shared 0.1 threshold. The original datasets' stated configurations largely remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V4 adds reversal-recovery analysis, a five-attribute compositional stress test, SD3 portability evaluation, and graph-recovery/convergence studies (Appendices E.4 and G). The original regularizer, guidance-scale, DDIM-step, and attention-guidance ablations remain. V1's classifier-failure case study and accompanying Figure 26 are removed.

E5.justification: V4 adds standard deviations to the CelebA results and explicitly reports three-seed means and standard deviations for its methods in Table 12. V1 supplied CelebA point estimates without a run count. ADNI uncertainty reporting remains. This establishes expanded reporting, not an explicitly documented increase from a known earlier run count.

E6.justification: V4 adds CelebA-HQ, reversal, intervention-identity, SD3, and graph-recovery results. CelebA values also change: FID without attention guidance moves from 8.509 to 8.152, and with attention guidance from 5.386 to 5.213, now accompanied by uncertainty. These are revised statistical reports, not established same-setting performance gains. Pendulum, ADNI, and original sensitivity-table values are retained.

T1.justification: The core SCM definitions and causal, PAI, and CTC equations remain substantively equivalent. The new identifiability discussion is qualitative and explicitly supplies no formal guarantee. The graph-learning extension describes an algorithmic penalty without adding a formal derivation, theorem, proof, or counterexample.

C1.justification: The abstract and listed contributions retain the same central claims: a modular frozen-backbone adapter, PAI/CTC regularization, faithful attribute interventions, and identity preservation. The headline Pendulum and ADNI improvements are unchanged. The added experiments principally strengthen support for these retained claims.

C2.justification: New Appendices F and G discuss approximate inversion, information loss, the absence of formal identifiability guarantees, reliance on a supplied graph, and difficulties recovering graphs from observational data. V4 distinguishes empirical reversibility from theoretical identification. Conversely, it removes v1's specific warning that classifiers can misjudge unusual counterfactuals such as bearded female faces.

D1.justification: V4 extends Table 5 with CelebA-HQ configurations, expands the algorithm explanation, and documents SD3 conditioning/inference and graph initialization/threshold choices. Existing hardware and core training details remain. The promise to release experimental code upon acceptance is removed without replacement access information.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds targeted discussion of Chao's diffusion causal mechanisms, Lyu's concept adapter, and Yeganeh's medical editing. Additional references support SD3, FlowEdit, identifiability, and causal discovery. The established positioning against VAE/GAN models, diffusion SCMs, and prompt-based editing remains largely intact.

P1.justification: Much of the introduction and method prose remains closely matched. V4 removes the introductory T2I primer, expands the appendix algorithm explanation, and relocates detailed CelebA/ADNI results and discussion to Appendix E. End matter is reorganized, with limited wording and header changes.

P2.justification: V4 changes the main text and references to two columns, compresses main-result tables, and splits or redisplays full tables in the appendices. Several figures are rearranged, the main ADNI illustration is shortened, and substantial new reversal, compositional, SD3, and graph-learning displays are added. The old classifier-failure figure is removed.

improvement.justification: V4 substantially strengthens validation through a CelebA-HQ comparison with DiffCounter, a second generative backbone, and direct reversal and identity-preservation measurements—important support missing from v1's single-backbone evaluation. CelebA uncertainty reporting and explicit identifiability qualifications further improve evidential quality. These gains outweigh removal of the classifier caveat and code-release commitment. Reporting still needs correction: for example, the claimed 79% CelebA FID reduction from 27.861 to 8.152 is approximately 71%.
